newsitem.title: FRANCE: French court to ponder top ETA extraditions.
newsitem.headline: French court to ponder top ETA extraditions.

text.p: A French court on Wednesday set March 5 for the extradition hearings of two top Spanish Basque separatist guerrillas now serving jail terms in France, justice sources said.

They said the Paris appeals court will hear requests for the extradition to Spain of several ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) guerrillas including Julian "Pototo" Achurra Egurola, 37, and Idoia "Tigress" Lopez Riano, 32.
"Pototo", believed to have been one of the bloody guerrilla group's three top leaders, was captured in France last July and jailed for three years last October on conspiracy charges.

He was said to be in charge of the logistics of ETA, which has killed some 800 people in a three-decade campaign for a separate Basque state. Spain had issued various warrants for his arrest on charges of murdering policemen and staging bomb attacks.
Lopez Riano, nicknamed the Tigress, is said to be among the most ruthless ETA guerrillas and is wanted in Spain in connection with 23 murders, including those of 16 paramilitary civil guards.
She was detained in France three years ago and jailed for five years on conspiracy and weapons charges.
Despite a French crackdown on ETA and the arrest of several of its leaders in recent years, Spanish authorities say the group's re-built leadership is still sheltering in France.
In a fresh wave of violence, ETA is being held responsible for six murders in Spain since the beginning of this year, including that of a Supreme Court judge.
A bomb exploded outside a Finance Ministry building in the French Basque resort of Hendaye before dawn, causing heavy damage but no injuries, a local government spokesman said.

No-one immediately claimed responsibility for the attack. The spokesman said it appeared to be the work of Iparretarrak (Those of the North) French Basque separatist guerrillas who have been sporadically active on the French side of the border.
The device, which appeared to be a 13-kilo (28 lb) gas canister, was planted outside the building, a former hotel which was due to open in May as a holiday centre for Finance Ministry staff.
